How a Term Covers Its Own Hyperparameters

Source: R/hyper.R
term_search.Rd

"grid" for every combination of the term's kinked hyperparameters, "cyclic" for one at a time. A term that names neither is covered the way the fitting layer covers one by default.

Usage

term_search(term, ...)

Arguments

term

A term, built or not.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A named list, one entry per penalty of the term, each a single string. Empty where the term names none.

Details

It matters only for a term carrying MORE THAN ONE hyperparameter with a kink – enet, scad and mcp – since there is nothing to combine otherwise. Under "grid" the cost is the product of the term's own grids and under "cyclic" their sum per pass.

Between two terms the sweep alternates whichever each one names, so y ~ lasso(X) + enet(R) costs the two blocks added and not multiplied, and one term asking for a product does not make the other pay for it.

See also

term_grid, term_path_min

Examples

term_search(enet(~x, search = "cyclic"))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "cyclic"
#> 
term_search(enet(~x))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "grid"
#>
